question: How has Jamaican inflation changed since 2020?

answer.headline: Jamaica inflation rose sharply to a 2022 peak of 10.35% before easing to 4% by 2025, averaging 6.22% over 2020–2025.

claims.text: Jamaica's inflation rate stood at 5.23% in 2020, the starting point of the period.
Inflation edged up by 0.63 pp to 5.86% in 2021.
Inflation surged by 4.49 pp to a period peak of 10.35% in 2022, the largest single-year jump in the series.
Inflation then fell sharply, declining 3.88 pp to 6.47% in 2023 — the largest annual decrease in the period.
Disinflation continued, with inflation easing 1.06 pp to 5.41% in 2024.
By 2025, inflation had declined a further 1.41 pp to 4%, the lowest reading in the series.
Across 2020–2025, Jamaica's inflation averaged 6.22%.
Overall, the series shows a single peak in 2022 followed by three consecutive years of disinflation through 2025.

gaps: No data is provided for years before 2020, so the pre-pandemic inflation baseline is unknown.
No breakdown by inflation sub-components (e.g., food, energy, core) is included.
No underlying drivers (exchange rate, monetary policy, global commodity prices) are evidenced here.
No comparison to other Caribbean economies or regional averages is provided.
Source publication date and any subsequent revisions to the 2024 and 2025 figures are not documented.

The 2015–2024 period average for the current account balance is 191.95 US$ mn (D:GY:current_account).

question: Which Caribbean economies have the highest debt burdens?

answer.headline: Cross-country comparison of gross government debt (% of GDP) in the Caribbean is limited to five economies in the retrieved evidence; BB carries the heaviest load, BS the lightest.

claims.text: Across 2015–2025, BB carries the heaviest gross government debt burden among the five economies retrieved, with a period average of 112.04% of GDP and a peak of 134.6% in 2017.
BS has the lightest debt burden among the retrieved economies, with a period average of 68.24% of GDP and a low of 49.9% in 2015.
AG and AW show similar period averages of 83.75% and 82.31% of GDP respectively, both well below BB but above BS and BZ (74.92%).
All five retrieved economies show a sharp 2020 COVID-era debt spike. The largest jump was AW at +44.20 pp, followed by BB at +28.00 pp, BZ at +24.40 pp, BS at +11.60 pp, and AG at +18.90 pp.
BB also shows a notable pre-pandemic jump, rising +7.50 pp in 2017 (to 134.6%), before a large -27.40 pp drop in 2018 (to 107.2%).
By 2025 projections, AW is forecast to fall to 63.6% (the lowest endpoint among the five), while BB remains highest at 94.2%. AG, BS, and BZ converge near 67.9–73.8%.

Methodological caveat: IMF WEO series are used here for cross-country comparability. For BB (2024) the Central Bank of Barbados reports a higher gross-debt ratio (e.g. 103% vs IMF 98.9%) on a different GDP base; for BS (2024) the Central Bank of The Bahamas reports 81.5% vs IMF 73.8%.

gaps: The retrieved evidence contains gross government debt (% of GDP) only for AG, AW, BB, BS, and BZ. No IMF WEO series for this indicator was returned for CW, DM, GD, GY, HT, JM, KN, KY, LC, SR, TC, TT, VC, or VG — though the retrieval hub notes the indicator is carried for TT, GY, JM, SR, GD, LC, KN, DM, VC, and HT, those series were not included in the evidence passed here and therefore cannot be cited.

question: Compare debt-to-GDP across Jamaica, Barbados, and Guyana.

answer.headline: Barbados carries the highest gross government debt-to-GDP ratio of the three over 2015–2025, with Guyana consistently well below Jamaica and Barbados; all three posted a sharp 2020 spike, and 2024 estimates sit below 2015 levels in each case.

claims.text: The 2015–2025 period average for gross government debt as % of GDP is highest in Barbados (112.04%), followed by Jamaica (86.22%), and is far below in Guyana (34.13%).
Each country registered a sharp 2020 increase in the ratio: Barbados +28.00 pp, Jamaica +13.60 pp, and Guyana +13.20 pp versus 2019.
By 2024 (IMF estimate), each country's ratio is below its 2015 level: Barbados 98.9 vs 122.5, Jamaica 62.5 vs 115.9, and Guyana 24.3 vs 42.2.
Barbados's ratio peaked at 134.6% in 2017 before falling -27.40 pp in 2018 to 107.2% in 2018.
For 2025, IMF projections diverge: Guyana rises +4.30 pp to 28.6% and Jamaica rises +5.20 pp to 67.7%, while Barbados continues to fall -4.70 pp to 94.2%.
For Barbados, the IMF WEO series is used; the Central Bank of Barbados reports a higher gross-debt ratio (e.g. 103% for 2024 vs IMF 98.9%) on a different GDP base.
Guyana's lowest level in the series is 24.3% in 2024, well under half of Jamaica's 24-year estimate of 62.5% and a fraction of Barbados's 98.9%.

gaps: No pre-2015 historical data is provided, so the long-run path into the 2015 baseline is not covered.
